items.title: User-history sparsity and benchmark coverage

source.label: Baseline run dataset snapshot

metricDefinitions.label: Eligible user
metricDefinitions.definition: A user with at least three distinct restaurant interactions, as required by the seen-user leave-last-two-out split.

metricDefinitions.label: Interaction count
metricDefinitions.definition: The number of deduplicated user-restaurant interactions in the immutable modeling snapshot.

filters: Interaction grain: first observed user-restaurant pair
caveats: The primary benchmark excludes users with fewer than three interactions, so its results do not represent the full observed user population.

evidenceFlow.title: Population calculation
evidenceFlow.detail: Count interactions by user, then classify users as 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5+ interactions and compute the share with at least three interactions.

evidenceFlow.title: Reconciliation
evidenceFlow.detail: The five history buckets sum to 6,987 users and the 3+ buckets sum to 2,396 benchmark-eligible users.

preview.note: Complete aggregate distribution derived from all 6,987 users in the snapshot.

assumptions: Five or more interactions is treated as the practical threshold for a relatively informative user history in this comparison.

items.title: Candidate cutoff value and recall

source.label: Baseline test candidates and metrics

metricDefinitions.label: Candidate Recall@K
metricDefinitions.definition: Among relevant test queries, the share whose held-out restaurant appears within the first K RRF candidates.

metricDefinitions.label: Final Recall@K
metricDefinitions.definition: Among relevant test queries, the share whose held-out restaurant appears within the first K LambdaMART predictions.

caveats: K=100 is an internal candidate budget, not a user-visible recommendation-list size.
The held-out label is the next observed review interaction, not necessarily the user's complete real-world next visit.

evidenceFlow.title: Recall calculation
evidenceFlow.detail: For each relevant test query, find the held-out restaurant's candidate rank and average the indicator rank <= K.

evidenceFlow.title: Published metric reconciliation
evidenceFlow.detail: Recomputed E3 Recall@20, @50, and @100 exactly match metrics.json.

preview.note: Complete set of evaluated cutoffs for this analysis.

assumptions: A candidate cutoff is decision-useful when interpreted together with its share of the catalog, retrieval latency, and the fixed final recommendation cutoff.
